data.content_ref: inline:The problem explicitly asks 'which of the TWO properties does an append-only event log actually require of its writers to survive at-least-once delivery' — idempotent or safe. SRC_001 refuses to answer this, claiming neither RFC property applies and proposing a third 'sequence-level' property. But per-operation idempotence is precisely sufficient: each retried append, keyed by a deduplication token, has 'the same effect as one' — RFC 9110's exact definition. The 'sequence-level composition' SRC_001 describes is just the result of composing per-operation idempotent writes with content addressing; it is not a categorically different property. SRC_001's own countercondition concedes that RFC idempotence is defined 'per-method,' which is exactly the right granularity for individual log writers. The target sidesteps the question posed rather than answering it.
